a.concept: SKIN LAB / SPEC SHEET. The email reads like covered's homepage turned into a technical data sheet for the offer. A corner-bracket frame holds a 3-line Archivo 800 headline at 125% width: "−30%" in signal yellow (true U+2212 minus), "LA 2" solid, and "SKINURI." outlined. Mono tags straddle the frame edges like the site's hero callouts: "● ORICARE 2 SKINURI", "● ORICE TELEFON" and "● AUTOMAT ÎN COȘ". Below the frame an equation panel sits on a 32px hairline grid with an amber glow: SKIN 01 (Samsung Titanium) + SKIN 02 (iPhone OFF Burgundy) = −30% LA AMBELE · AUTOMAT ÎN COȘ. It shows the "mix brands, any phone" mechanic without a paragraph of explanation. Every following section has the homepage's numbered mono index (01–06) with a yellow meter line, an eyebrow with a yellow dot, and an uppercase H2 ending in a period. Section 01 is a ruled spec table: PRODUSE / TELEFON / COD / EXEMPLU / NU INTRĂ. Its worked example is the cart-tested 2 × Negru Mat, RON 138.00 → RON 96.60. Product cards are spec cards: a light warm-grey image well like the site, the sale pill, a mono finish tag plus rating, the title, the price with the struck compare-at price, and a mini offer block on each card ("% RON 48.30 / buc. când iei 2"). That block echoes the PDP cv-offer card, at 0.7 × the price, which is the site's own formula. The email closes on the device-picker tiles and a black footer with the company ID table and a 'covered' watermark.

key_moves: The hero headline is set like the site's 'ÎMBRACĂ-ȚI / TELEFONUL.': '−30%' at 132px in yellow, then 'LA 2', then 'SKINURI.' outlined. The outline is progressive enhancement: inside @supports, -webkit-text-stroke 2px #F3F3EF over a #0A0A0B fill, with a solid #F3F3EF fallback. I verified the fallback in a render with all <style> blocks stripped.
Corner brackets are built from 1px #50504F border cells. Each arm sits at the midline of a 24px tag row, so the mono tags straddle the frame edge as on the homepage, using tables and no positioning.

The SKIN 01 + SKIN 02 equation panel pairs a Samsung and an iPhone (OFF Burgundy, the site's most-pushed new finish). The hairline grid and amber glow are background-image enhancement on a #111113 fallback.

Each product card is split into four table rows across the pair: image well, tag and title, price, offer chip. Titles, prices and offer chips therefore line up across the two columns whatever the title length. Cards stay 2-up on mobile at about 160px each.
Every card repeats the PDP offer card as a mini spec line: a yellow % circle and 'RON X / buc. când iei 2' (0.7 × the live price). On mobile '/ buc. când iei 2' moves to its own line.

Section 01 turns the offer mechanics into a spec table. It uses only verified facts: no code, any phone, brands can be mixed, 2 of the same skin works, huse/folie/extraopțiuni are excluded, and the cart-tested example 138.00 → 96.60.

Copy reuses the site's own lines: 'Zero volum, stil maxim.', 'Cifrele care ne recomandă.', 'Un singur finisaj e rareori de ajuns.', the USP texts verbatim, 'Alege-ți telefonul', 'Vezi skinuri'. The closing line 'Alege modelul. Alege două finisaje.' is adapted from the site's 'Alege modelul, alege finisajul.'
I re-checked all 15 product prices live on 2026-10-06 via /products/<handle>.js. All match the research and all are available. Prices use the site format 'RON 69.00'.

Getting from 127 KB to 87.8 KB: the body font is set once on the wrapper and inherits, the mono stack is set on container tables, card side borders, pill layout and the % circle moved to <style> classes, spacer cells were simplified and the whitespace between tags collapsed.

render.sh at 375 is wrong. Headless Chrome on Windows keeps a window about 500px wide, so the page lays out at ~500px and the shot is clipped. That output is kept as drafts/variant-a-375-rendersh.png. If <style> is stripped (e.g. Gmail with non-Google accounts): the outline falls back to solid white, the fonts fall back to Arial Black / Helvetica / Consolas, card side borders and pill/chip-circle padding are lost, the radial tile gradient goes, and the hover states go. The layout still holds; I verified this with a stripped render.
Light product image wells (#EFEFEB) may be darkened by Gmail iOS or Outlook forced dark mode. Only Outlook.com gets a [data-ogsb] guard.
Outlook desktop shows square corners. Only the hero primary button has a VML fallback; the closing button is a plain bulletproof table.

Image weight is about 1.5–2 MB in total (transparent PNGs; the Samsung Titanium hero image is about 195 KB at width=400). Shopify ignores format=jpg for these files, and converting would lose transparency anyway.

The descriptive lines for OFF Silver and DUO Pink, and the note 'Scorul mediu dat de clienți.' under 4,69/5, are my wording based on what the product images and data show; they are not site copy. 'Primești acest e-mail pentru că ești abonat la newsletterul covered.' is standard compliance text.
'Retur în 30 de zile' is the homepage USP used verbatim. The refund policy says sale items can't be returned, a conflict the site itself already has.
The OFF Burgundy MAT variant (linked from the hero) is sold out; LUCIOS is in stock. The research noted products were being edited on 2026-10-06, so prices should be rechecked right before sending.

a.self_critique: Strong on brand fidelity: palette, Archivo/Martian Mono roles, eyebrow dots, the yellow meter indices, the outlined hero word, the yellow band, the light product wells and the footer ID table all match covered.ro. The offer is explained by structure (the equation panel, the spec table, an offer chip on every card) rather than by marketing paragraphs. Weaknesses: the email is long (about 7.7k px desktop, 8k px mobile) because it has 6 numbered sections plus the closing block. The hero leaves empty black space to the right of 'LA 2' on desktop; a small mono annotation there could tighten it. The two hero phone renders read at slightly different scales because the source PNGs crop differently. The Samsung best-seller row is visually monotone (mostly black finishes), which is what really sells but looks heavy. Hitting the size budget meant moving some decorative styling into classes, so clients without <style> get a plainer but intact version. The 4,69/5 stat cell's note is my wording.

Between sections, a slim yellow band in the style of the site's marquee (double #C18C02 rules) repeats the offer with verified variations. The closing CTA echoes the site's "60.000+ SKINURI REALIZATE. AL TĂU URMEAZĂ." with the hero's outlined-text treatment and a dark copy of the PDP offer card, then the stats row.

key_moves: The offer panel copies the site's own yellow 'Ofertă pachet' tile (◆ eyebrow, huge −30%, LA 2 SKINURI, ruler ticks, verbatim subtext) and scales it up as the hero.

The worked example only uses math the research verified in the cart: test (b), iPhone Negru Mat RON 69.00 → 48.30 plus Samsung Burgundy RON 89.00 → 62.30, total RON 158.00 → RON 110.60, savings RON 47.40. It is laid out like the site's cart, and both products are linked.

Each card carries its own 2-skin price chip, 'RON X / buc.' at 0.7 × the current price, matching the site's PDP 'când iei 2' line. Values were checked against the PDP figures in the research (48.30, 62.30, 63.00, 69.30, 84.00).

Every price, compare-at price and availability flag was re-fetched from /products/<handle>.js today and all matched. All image URLs return 200 image/png at &width=400, and all link targets return 200.

Cards copy the site's collection grid: light radial tile behind the cutout phone (bgcolor #EFEFEB fallback), floored ASCII '-NN%' pill, ★ CEL MAI VÂNDUT / ● NOU pills, mono index, yellow mono price with <s> compare-at. On mobile the best-seller pill shrinks to ★ and the compare-at price drops to its own line, so rows stay aligned.
Real minus sign U+2212 in −30% and ASCII hyphen in the sale badges, as the site does. Prices use the site's 'RON 69.00' format, not 'lei'.
Outlined text is a progressive enhancement: the solid #F3F3EF fill is inline and the stroke sits inside @supports(-webkit-text-stroke), so clients that strip it never end up with transparent text.

Fluid hybrid layout: 100%/max-width 600 container with an MSO ghost table, percentage 2-up grids that work without media queries, bulletproof buttons with mso-padding-alt, an mso Arial override, and bgcolor plus inline background-color on every dark or yellow surface.

Final size 87,528 bytes (about 85.5 KB) after compaction: font inheritance, card-level mono family, divs inside cards, and the model tiles collapsed into one row. All 53 covered.ro links carry utm_source=email&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=30-la-2-skinuri&utm_content=<section>.

Offer copy goes beyond the headline only where cart tests prove it: FĂRĂ COD (automatic discount), a 3rd skin is also −30% (test d), iPhone + Samsung mixes (test b), and huse/folie excluded (tests c1–c3). There are no dates, codes, stock claims or free-shipping claims.

The 640 render was taken at 7600px tall because the email is about 7.4k px and the requested 6000px would cut off the footer.

Samsung grid has 4 cards, not 6, to stay under 90 KB (the brief allows 4–6). It skips best-seller #2 'Skin Samsung - Personalizat' because the FAQ says personalised products have no ramburs and no returns, which would contradict the USP strip. It shows ranks 1, 3, 4 and 5.

The trust strip uses 'Retur în 30 de zile – Pentru produsele nefolosite…' as the homepage and PDP state it. The formal refund policy says sale items cannot be returned, and every skin is technically on sale. Legal or the merchant should confirm before sending.

Prices were re-verified on 2026-10-06, but research saw products being edited that morning. Re-check prices, the compare-at for OFF Silver (currently none), and the 199/138 collection counts just before sending.

The 'VEZI TOATE SKINURILE' ghost CTA links to /pages/categorii-produse (the site's SKIN-URI hub). The hero and closing 'ALEGE-ȚI TELEFONUL' go to the homepage, where the device picker lives, because there is no verified anchor URL for the picker itself.

Web fonts (Archivo with the width axis, Martian Mono) only load in Apple Mail and iOS Mail. Gmail and Outlook fall back to Arial Black / Arial and Courier New, so the wide look is lost there. Headings were sized with room to spare for this.
The decorative ruler, radial tile gradients, amber glow and hover states are class-based. Clients that strip <style>, such as Gmail with non-Google accounts, fall back to flat colours with no ruler.
ESP click-tracking will rewrite the 63 links and add roughly 5–7 KB. At about 85.5 KB the email should still stay under Gmail's 102 KB clip, but check the final size after the ESP pass.
Footer subscription line ('Primești acest e-mail pentru că te-ai abonat la newsletterul covered.') is standard compliance wording, not copy taken from the site.
b.self_critique: Strongest parts: the yellow hero reads as covered's own offer tile, not a generic sale banner. The receipt turns "−30% la 2 skinuri" into concrete, verified lei-off. The per-card "RON X / buc. când iei 2" chip keeps the offer in front of the reader in every grid, and the cards are close to pixel-faithful copies of the site's collection cards. Weaker parts: the email is long (about 7.4k px desktop) and somewhat repetitive. Three grids of near-identical cards plus two strips could feel heavy, and dropping one strip or the Noutăți model row would tighten it. The giant −30% and the outline only show their real character in Apple Mail; in Gmail it will look more generic, with Arial Black and Courier mono. The dark phones (Negru Mat, Honeycomb, ULTRA Matte) rely on the light tile for contrast, so they look flatter in clients that drop the radial-gradient class. Single-line card titles leave a small gap above the price, a side effect of the fixed title height that keeps paired cards aligned.

Each section ends with the device-picker "VEZI TOATE SKINURILE …" bar, showing the real counts 199 and 138. NOUTĂȚI is framed as "DROP-URILE NOI." AL TĂU URMEAZĂ.", and the black site footer with the faint "covered" watermark.

The footer watermark depends on a media query to shrink to 64px on mobile. Where media queries are unsupported, it relies on overflow:hidden on a div to avoid widening the layout.
c.self_critique: This is the most brand-faithful of the directions I could build. Hero type, cards, pills, see-all bars, the band, stats and footer all reuse measured site tokens and verbatim copy, and the offer mechanics are fully explicit without inventing anything. Weaknesses: the email is long (about 7,000px desktop and 7,850px mobile). The hero phones are flat and untilted, so they read less dynamic than the site's fan. Three dark phones in the iPhone grid (Dark, Negru Mat, Black Titanium) make it look tonally monotonous, because I followed the true best-seller ranking over visual variety. The ticket's notch circles are a small, Apple-first flourish that degrades to squares in Outlook. With more time I would test a 6-product variant against a shorter cut, and look at a composite hero image if the client can host one.
